title: Handshake to Habit: Onboarding Roadmap & 30/60/90 Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This lightweight playbook is designed to convert an initial customer handshake into habitual product usage within 90 days. It bundles a pragmatic checklist, measurable outcomes, risk triggers, and templated emails/meeting agendas that CSMs can adapt. The goal is to increase time-to-value (TTV), reduce early churn risk, and build replicable success motions for mid-market customers integrating Redwood Inference.

Audience:
- CSMs managing self-serve and sales-assisted accounts (ARR <$250k)
- Solutions engineers supporting first launches
- Onboarding ops for playbook automation and templating

Core principles:
- Outcomes first: start from the single metric the customer cares about (latency SLOs met, inference cost reduction, first production flow live).
- Small wins early: schedule quick wins in week 1 to show tangible value.
- Repeatable rituals: 30/60/90 check-ins with clear owner actions.
- Escalate early: surface risk signals fast and route to SE/Platform/Support.

Success criteria (choose 1–3 per account):
- Production inference flow processing 10K tokens/day with <200ms p50 latency
- 20% unit cost reduction vs baseline via batching/quantization in 90 days
- First internal app using embeddings in production and passing user acceptance tests

Pre-boarding (before Day 0 - Handshake)
- Deliverables to customer: onboarding checklist PDF, brief Runbook template, account-specific kickoff invite with agenda
- Internal: assign CSM, tag account in CRM, create onboarding board (Jira ticket or Asana), share access with SE and Solutions
- Validate: customer has identified primary use-case, integration owner, and success metric

Day 0–7 (Week 1): Establish momentum
Objectives:
- Kickoff meeting: align objectives, communication cadence, and success metrics (30 min + recording)
- Quick wins: verify API key connectivity, run a basic inference test, confirm access to model catalog
- Runbook: deliver a two-page runbook with escalation contacts and a minimal test plan

Checklist (Week 1):
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled and recorded
- [ ] API call validation (sample prompt executed)
- [ ] Baseline telemetry collection enabled (latency/cost/availability)
- [ ] Identify primary app owner and integration technical lead
- [ ] Shared Slack channel or email thread created

Owner actions (CSM/SE):
- CSM: confirm business metric and stakeholder map
- SE: validate environment (hosted/dedicated/private), confirm sample model and sequence lengths
- Onboarding Ops: provision trial credits or test capacity if needed

Day 8–30 (Weeks 2–4): Move from test to repeatable flow
Objectives:
- Implement initial integration with one production-like endpoint
- Start basic observability dashboards (tokens, p50/p95 latency, error rate)
- Run a short performance smoke test and document results

Checklist (Day 8–30):
- [ ] Prod-like endpoint created and isolated from dev keys
- [ ] Observability dashboard shared with customer (or access granted)
- [ ] First runbook-driven smoke test executed and results recorded
- [ ] Two optimization experiments proposed (batching, KV caching, quantization profiles)
- [ ] Midpoint check-in scheduled (30-day review)

Owner actions:
- SE: implement smoke test, propose optimization variants with expected impact
- CSM: align the customer on the next milestones and gather feedback on blockers

Metric targets by Day 30 (example):
- Telemetry baseline collected over 3–5 test runs
- One optimization experiment queued for pilot

Day 31–60 (Weeks 5–8): Trial optimizations and guardrails
Objectives:
- Run optimization pilots, measure impact on cost and latency
- Harden security and access controls (key rotation, IP allowlists for Hosted/Dedicated)
- Train internal end-users on basic console/usage patterns

Checklist (Day 31–60):
- [ ] Optimization pilot run #1 completed and evaluated
- [ ] Cost delta and latency delta documented
- [ ] Security checklist completed (at least 3 controls verified)
- [ ] Internal enablement session delivered for 1–2 engineering champions
- [ ] Renewal/reach-back signal configured in CRM (e.g., usage threshold for outreach)

Owner actions:
- CSM: run adoption workshop, collect NPS-style feedback on onboarding experience
- SE: iterate on model config and recommend routing policy if cross-region testing needed
- Product Ops: capture any missing console feature that blocks adoption

Decision gate (end of Day 60):
- Go/no-go to expand to additional use-cases or to throttle back to pilot mode. Document the decision and next steps.

Day 61–90 (Weeks 9–13): Expand and operationalize
Objectives:
- Promote the integration to broader internal users or scale throughput targets
- Finalize governance (SLAs, runbooks, incident playbooks)
- Prepare renewal/expansion play materials if appropriate

Checklist (Day 61–90):
- [ ] Production traffic steady for 7–14 days with agreed SLOs met
- [ ] Cost-per-token target hit or plan established
- [ ] At least one internal team trained and self-sufficient
- [ ] QBR scheduled and success pack prepared

Owner actions:
- CSM: assemble success pack (metrics vs. target, qualitative testimonials, next-phase recommendations)
- SE: handover runbook and on-call rotations / escalation matrix to SRE or support
- Solutions: propose expansion patterns (additional endpoints, model variants)

90-day artifacts to deliver to customer:
- 90-day success pack PDF (baseline, experiments, outcomes, recommended next steps)
- Operational Runbook (keys, endpoints, rollback steps, contacts)
- Training recording and short FAQ

Risk signals & escalation path:
- Low usage in first 14 days => CS owner outreach and friction log required
- High error rate (>3% 5xx or model failures) => SE deep-dive and potential P0 support case
- Cost blowout (>30% above estimates) => pause experiments and engage Optimize team

Templates (paste-friendly snippets)
- Kickoff agenda (30 min): intros (5), goals & success metric (10), technical owner walkthrough (10), next steps (5)
- 30-day check-in subject line: "30-day check-in: metrics snapshot & next experiments"
- Escalation note: "Observed X errors in Y timeframe — requesting SE triage and temporary routing to fallback model"

Automations & playbook integrations (ops notes)
- Add a CRM automation to create a JIRA onboarding board on Deal Stage -> Contract Signed
- Slack: auto-create #cust-<shortname>-onboarding channel when onboarding board created
- Monitoring: add onboarding tag in telemetry so we can compare adoption cohorts

Open questions / backlog items:
- Standardize how we calculate cost-savings for pilot customers (single formula or per-account adjustments?)
- Shorten time to first smoke test for Private deployments with prescriptive checklist for network teams
- Create lightweight post-90-day "health check" for customers that scaled past initial pilot

Notes to self / for CSMs:
- Keep meeting agendas tight — aim to leave with 1–2 clear action items every meeting
- Record everything: screenshots of dashboards are gold for the 90-day success pack
- If stuck on infra/network in Private, escalate to Platform Eng with clear repro steps and packet captures

Appendix: Quick email templates
- Welcome email (post-sign): "Thank you for choosing Redwood Inference — attached is a short checklist and the kickoff invite. Please add your integration lead and we’ll run a 30-minute kickoff to align outcomes."
- 30-day reminder: "Quick update: we’ve run baseline tests and propose two optimization experiments next week. Can you confirm a 30-minute slot to review results?"

End of document.
